title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Priya Singh
body:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood's security and compliance controls relevant to: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC gates, incident response security procedures, evidence collection workflows for audits, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended as the canonical operational reference for engineering, security, and compliance stakeholders.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and supporting infrastructure (control plane, telemetry, build systems).
- Includes human access, service-to-service auth, and automated evidence workflows used for external audits (SOC2, ISO27001).

Ownership

- Document owner: Security (security@redwood.com)
- Primary owners by area:
  - RBAC & Auth: IAM and Platform teams
  - Audit Logging: Observability team
  - Data Residency & Retention: Compliance and Legal
  - Secure SDLC: Eng DX + Security

Key Principles

1) Least privilege by default. Roles grant the minimum permissions required to perform tasks; elevation is timeboxed.
2) Visibility: all access and privileged actions produce immutable audit records.
3) Data locality & retention are explicit and documented per customer and dataset classification.
4) Security gates are automated where possible (CI checks, policy-as-code) and manual sign-offs are auditable.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Overview

Redwood uses centralized Identity and Access Management. Workforce access is via SSO (Okta). Service identities are short-lived where possible (OIDC tokens, workload identity) and long-lived keys are limited and rotated.

Roles and role-mapping (overview table)

| Role | Scope | Typical Membership | Privilege Examples |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Viewer | Org-level read | All staff | Read-only dashboards, tickets |
| Developer | Project level | Engineers | Deploy to staging, read logs, create feature branches |
| Platform-Infra | Org infra | Infra team | Manage clusters, change infra config |
| SRE-Operator | Runtime | SRE team | Trigger rollbacks, adjust autoscale |
| Security-Admin | Security controls | Security team | Manage detection rules, access reviews |
| Billing-Admin | Billing data | Finance | Access billing reports |

Authentication & MFA

- SSO: Okta + OIDC for Redwood accounts (all humans).
- MFA: Required for all workforce accounts (hardware token OR TOTP + biometrics where supported).
- Conditional access: Block access from unmanaged devices unless explicitly approved.

Service-to-service Auth

- Prefer workload identity (OIDC) with short TTL tokens (<=1h) issued by the internal token broker.
- For external integrators where short-lived tokens are not feasible, issue scoped API keys with constrained permissions and automated tracking.
- Service account keys: rotate every 30 days for high-privilege accounts, 90 days for lower-privilege where automated rotation is supported.
- Keys must be stored in KMS/HSM backed secret stores and accessed via authenticated identity tokens.

Access Review & Just-in-time (JIT) Elevation

- Quarterly automated access reviews for high-risk groups (Platform-Infra, Security-Admin, SRE-Operator).
- JIT elevation implemented for high-privilege tasks: request via CLI/Portal, approval logged, automatic revocation after a configured TTL (default 2 hours).

2) Audit Logging

Purpose

Ensure immutable evidence of who did what, when, and from where. Audit logs feed detection, forensics, compliance reporting, and retrospective reviews.

What is logged

- Workforce authentication events (login, MFA challenge, device)
- Role changes and access requests (create/update/delete role bindings)
- Privileged actions (deployments to production, config changes, secret access)
- Data export events (bulk exports, admin queries returning PII)
- System events (service restarts, auto-scaling events, kernel-level alerts where applicable)

Retention & Storage

- Critical audit events (authn/authz changes, admin ops, data exports): retained 3 years (immutable).
- Standard audit logs (application and platform events): retained 1 year by default.
- Aggregated telemetry for product analytics: retained 90 days unless tagged for longer retention.
- Storage: Write-once S3 buckets with object-lock for critical audit events; backups replicated across regions for high-availability.

Log Integrity & Access Controls

- All audit logs are signed at ingestion with a write-only signing key stored in HSM.
- Access to raw audit logs is restricted to Security and SRE roles, read access granted via timeboxed request and audited.

Alerting and Monitoring

- High-priority alerts (failed privilege escalations, unexpected exfil events): page Security on-call and SRE.
- Daily anomaly runs: automated scripts generate reports for the Security team (top unusual API key usage, cross-region data reads).

Example: retrieve critical audit events (CLI)

- Example (pseudo-CLI):
  redwood logs query --index=audit --filter "event:privileged_action AND since:24h" --format json 

3) Data Residency & Retention

Classification

- Data is classified at ingestion: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated (e.g., GDPR-sensitive, customer PII). Classification drives residency and retention rules.

Residency Controls

- Customer-facing deployments may be pinned to region(s). Control plane location is documented per customer contract.
- Cross-region backups for regulated customers require explicit approval and are encrypted in transit and at rest.

Retention Matrix (example)

| Data Type | Example Sources | Retention Default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Auth & Audit (critical) | Okta logs, admin ops | 3 years | Immutable, retention via S3 object-lock |
| Application logs (standard) | API requests | 1 year | PII should be redacted before long-term storage |
| Usage metrics | Telemetry pipeline | 90 days | Aggregated after 90 days |
| Backups | DB snapshots | 90 days | Longer for Dedicated customer contracts |

Deletion & Erasure (customer data)

- Erasure requests follow the Customer Data Erasure process: verify identity, determine data locations (index via metadata service), schedule deletion, and produce evidence (deletion job IDs and checksum). Typical SLA: 30 days to complete erasure unless backlog or regulatory holds.

4) Secure SDLC (Secure Software Development Life Cycle)

Gates and Automation

- Pull Request checks: static analysis (SAST), dependency vulnerability scanning (SCA), secret scanning, linting, and unit tests required.
- CI-only deploys to staging; production deploys require a signed promotion step and must pass security scans.
- Policy-as-code: RBAC policy changes and infra changes must pass policy linter (OPA/Conftest).

Manual Reviews & Sign-offs

- Security review required for: new data stores containing regulated data, changes to key management, changes to auth flows. Security sign-off is recorded in the PR and in the change log.

Supply Chain Controls

- Binaries published to production images: reproducible builds, cryptographic signing of artifacts.
- Dependency allowlist: automated build pipeline blocks builds that include blacklisted packages.

Secrets & Key Management

- No plaintext secrets in repos. Use vault-backed secret injection at build/runtime.
- Build system rotates signing keys every 180 days; emergency rotation runbook available.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Severity levels (security-focused)

- Sev-1 (Critical): Active exfiltration of customer data, production data corruption, key compromise.
- Sev-2 (High): Privilege escalation to high-privileged roles, confirmed active attacker activity without large-scale exfil.
- Sev-3 (Medium): Anomalous access patterns with limited scope, non-production security incidents.

Initial triage checklist (first 60 minutes)

1. Triage lead assigned (on-call Security).
2. Capture scope: affected services, estimated time window, potential data sets.
3. Isolate cause: disable compromised keys, revoke sessions, rotate affected secrets if immediate risk.
4. Preserve evidence: snapshot forensic images, collect audit log export (copy to immutable bucket), record chain-of-custody.
5. Notify stakeholders (internal): Exec comms, Legal, Compliance, Customer Success for impacted customers.

Forensics & Evidence Preservation

- Forensic images: follow the Forensics Playbook; capture memory and disk snapshots where possible and store in controlled evidence buckets.
- Audit log preservation: create a dedicated immutable export and lock retention to prevent tampering.

Communication & External Notifications

- Legal determines regulatory notification timelines (e.g., GDPR) in partnership with Security and Customer Success.
- Where applicable, coordinate public incident communications with PR and Legal.

Post-incident

- Root cause analysis and postmortem within 14 days (security postmortem template must be used).
- Action items tracked in JIRA and ownership assigned; security validation required before closure.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Audit evidence types

- Access control lists and role assignments (historical snapshots).
- Audit logs showing privileged actions and reviewer/approval records.
- Secure SDLC evidence: PRs with security sign-offs, SAST/SCA scan results, signed artifacts.
- Data residency/retention proof: metadata showing residency flags, retention job logs, deletion job IDs.

Automated evidence generation

- Evidence pipelines produce timeboxed exports for audits:
  - Access snapshot: redwood iam export --as-of 2026-01-01 --format csv
  - Audit log export: redwood logs export --index=audit --since=2025-01-01 --out s3://evidence-bucket/audit-2025-archive.zip

Evidence review & packaging

1. Security compiles evidence index (index.json) referencing export job IDs and checksums.
2. Compliance verifies and annotates items for auditors.
3. Upload to secure audit portal (S3 w/ restricted ACL + KMS key).

SLA for audit requests

- Internal: 5 business days for routine evidence requests.
- External auditors: 10 business days by contract unless expedited.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Exception request process

- Submit an Exception request (ServiceNow/Form): include affected asset, control being bypassed, duration requested, compensating controls, and risk assessment.
- Triage: Security reviews and assigns risk owner. For high-risk exceptions, a cross-functional review (Security, Infra, Legal, Product) is required.
- Approval matrix:
  - Low risk (temporary config change): Security approval sufficient for <=30 days.
  - Medium risk (privilege expansion affecting production): Security + Infra for <=90 days.
  - High risk (bypass of audit or KMS): Security + Infra + Legal + CTO for <=30 days; renewals require evidence of mitigation.

Timeboxed & Audited

- All exceptions are timeboxed and automatically expire. Renewal requires re-evaluation and new evidence.
- Exception records are included in quarterly risk reporting to the Exec Security Committee.

Appendix A — Runbooks & Commands

- Revoke user sessions (Okta CLI):
  okta sessions revoke --user alice@redwood.com

- Export privilege changes (example):
  redwood iam history --resource iam:role/platform-infra --since 2025-01-01 --format csv > platform_infra_role_history.csv

Appendix B — Contacts

- Security on-call: pager duty (link internal)
- Security leadership: security-leads@redwood.com
- Compliance: compliance@redwood.com

Appendix C — Glossary

- JIT: Just-in-time elevation
- KMS/HSM: Key Management Service / Hardware Security Module
- SCA/SAST: Software Composition Analysis / Static Application Security Testing
